Author_or_Organisation: Atungbou, N.

Author_or_Organisation: Longkumer, A.

Author_or_Organisation: Directorate of Information & Public Relations, Government of Mizoram

Author_or_Organisation: Sonowal, R.

Author_or_Organisation: Bhattacharya, B.; Chandra Deka, D.
Title: Preparation, physicochemical analysis and antioxidant properties of Rohi and Sepa: traditional rice beers of the Sonowal Kacharis, Assam
Publication_or_Source_Type: Peer-reviewed article, Indian Journal of Traditional Knowledge 25(9), 914–921

Author_or_Organisation: Das, R.; Medhi, M. C.; Tamang, B.

Publication_or_Source_Type: Peer-reviewed research article, AMB Express 16, article 91

Black Rohi Modh is recorded provisionally as a substrate-associated variant pending local terminology confirmation. Antioxidant assays and predicted pathways do not establish clinical benefits.

Author_or_Organisation: Talukdar, S.; Jyethi, D. S.; Sarma, B.; et al.

Author_or_Organisation: Ministry of Women and Child Development, Government of India
Title: An Exploratory Study on Indigenous Food of North-East India — Kesa mod/Jonga mod entry

Claims_Supported: Describes local rice, herbal yeast cake called bakhar, fermentation and extraction with a wooden device called Ruhi; resulting liquid is described as kesa mod.

Author_or_Organisation: Bhattacharya, B.; Deka, D. C.

Authors' comparisons to drinking-water metal limits do not establish that alcohol is safe overall.

Author_or_Organisation: Borah, D.; Gogoi, T.; Sarma, J.; Borah, P. J.; Gohain, B.; Mili, C.; Upadhyaya, A.; Basumatary, J.; Neog, K.; Wangpan, T.; Tangjang, S.

Reviewed main text does not name all 32 villages or map community/beverage to each district. Do not infer that every community or beverage occurs in every study district. Po:ro apong ash/extraction account is source-specific; separate generic distillation section is not explicitly identified as a Po:ro stage.

Author_or_Organisation: Senapati, S. S.; Gurumayum, S.

Communities_or_Beverages_Covered: Traditional beverage starter cultures and plant ingredients; comparative source for checking later review citations

Do not use broad plant claims as village-specific evidence or clinical proof of medicinal effects.

Author_or_Organisation: Bhuyan, B.; Baishya, K.

Claims_Supported: Synthesizes ethnomedicinal plants and traditional rice-beer/starter information across seven named communities; secondary cross-check for beverage terminology and selected localities

Confirm locality attribution against the article text and underlying sources.

Author_or_Organisation: Deka, A. K.; Basumatary, S.; Deka, D. C.

Claims_Supported: Reports interviews with 50 people and detailed methods for stored rice-based and fruit-based Bodo beverages, including ingredients, fermentation/storage periods, local vessel names and a traditional distillation setup

Author_or_Organisation: Kumari, S.; Ama, T.; Jyoti Koch, P.; Debbarma, R.

Publication_or_Source_Type: Original research article; Indian Journal of Traditional Knowledge 24(7):615–626

Communities_or_Beverages_Covered: Opo starter; Nyishi rice-wine varieties named Tisar, Kecha and Adak
Claims_Supported: Characterizes physicochemical and biochemical properties of traditional Nyishi rice-wine varieties; identifies Opo as the traditional starter culture and reports sample-specific differences among Tisar, Kecha and Adak.

Author_or_Organisation: Hoikhokim; Laldinthar, R.; Haokip, H.; Lhungdim, N.

Communities_or_Beverages_Covered: Anthom; sticky/glutinous rice, black or white varieties; starter called Chol; liquid fraction called aning
Claims_Supported: Documents Anthom as a fermented rice beverage and describes a source-specific process using cooked sticky rice, Chol starter, a covered vessel and fermentation for 3–7 days; the liquid fraction is called aning.
Limitations_or_Caveats: The paper reports ethnomedicinal uses as traditional claims, not clinical evidence. Village-level sampling and prevalence are not established in the accessible record; recipe and social-use descriptions should not be generalized to all Thadou-Kuki households.

Author_or_Organisation: Gogoi, P.; Konwar, S.; Das, S.; Das, D.; Doimari, R.; Sonar, T.; Doley, S.

Author_or_Organisation: Tiwari, S. C.; Mahanta, D.

Author_or_Organisation: Borah, Porismita
Title: Documentation of ethnobotanical plants used in the preparation of Apong, a traditionally prepared rice beer by the Mishing tribal community of Majuli district

Author_or_Organisation: Das, Santanu; Özkurt, Ezgi; Joishy, Tulsi Kumari; Mukherjee, Ashis K.; Hildebrand, Falk; Khan, Mojibur R.

Publication_or_Source_Type: Peer-reviewed research article; mSystems 8:e00745-23

Claims_Supported: Reports a seven-village survey used to screen potential volunteers and a final analysis cohort of 166 (142 Mising Apong consumers and 24 monk controls); methods identify participants from Telam, Dhemaji and Majuli districts. It does not name the seven villages in the accessible text or assign each beverage to individual villages. Health associations are observational and cannot establish causation or safety; alcohol consumption is not a health recommendation.

Author_or_Organisation: Das, Santanu; Deb, Dibyayan; Adak, Atanu; Khan, Mojibur R.

Laboratory analysis of selected samples is not a representative survey of all production. Health-related interpretation is exploratory and not proof of benefit or safety.

Full text was not accessible in this review; claims should be cross-checked against cited primary studies. Do not treat flavour/chemical discussion as evidence of clinical benefit or safety.

Author_or_Organisation: Pegu, Rajeswar; Gogoi, Jitu; Tamuli, Ajit K.; Teron, Robindra

Communities_or_Beverages_Covered: Nogin Apong; Po:ro Apong (saimod); E’pob starter; Ta:suk extraction; cultural and ethnobotanical knowledge
Claims_Supported: Documents traditional knowledge using discussions, semi-structured interviews and personal observations. Distinguishes Nogin Apong (fermented rice with E’pob) from Po:ro Apong (rice, usually glutinous, with ash of paddy husk and straw). Limitations_or_Caveats: Fieldwork is dated 2010 and 2012 and should be treated as historical, source-specific documentation. Reported community beliefs about health effects are not clinical evidence. Do not interpret filtration as distillation or assume this process is universal across all Mising localities.

Publication_or_Source_Type: Peer-reviewed open-access research article; Discover Food 6:376

Limitations_or_Caveats: Study-site districts are not a production census and do not establish village-level beverage attribution. Table 1 prints ST/EES/2024/015 for two taxa; verify against Arunachal University of Studies herbarium records. Community-reported medicinal uses are not clinical evidence; conservation effects are not established causally by the qualitative design. See research/assam/cross-community-2026-source-quality-audit.md and research/assam/src-091-voucher-audit.md.
